full_judgment:
5. The suit was decreed on contest against the defendant-appellants for a sum of Taka 7,55,22,686.61 with interest at the rate of Taka 20% from 1-10-1992 till realization of the decretal amount. The defendants were directed to pay the decretal amount within 90(ninety) days. 

 6. Since the defendants failed to pay the decretal amount, the decree-holder-Bank put the decree into execution in Title Execution Case No. 59 of 2003 for realization of the decretal dues along with the interest and costs amounting to Taka 22,35,053,00. In the execution case, advertisement was made in the newspaper for selling the mortgaged properties in auction and respondent No. 1, Jubak Housing and Real Estate Development Limited, on 11-4-2004, offered the highest bid at Taka 6,10,00,000. The Executing Court by order dated 11-4-2004 refused to accept the bid as it was considered to be too low. Challenging the said order, respondent No.1 filed Writ Petition No.2067 of 2004 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule Nisi absolute declaring the order dated 11-4-2004 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Jari Case No. 59 of 2003 (in the Rule issuing order and in the impugned judgment though it has been written as Artha Jari case, the order sheet shows it was registered as title execution case) to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 8. He further submits that having regard to the fact that the property of the judgment-debtor-petitioners is going to be sold in inadequate price, they were the necessary parties interested in the instant writ petition but the writ petitioner surreptitiously prayed for rule against the Artha Rin Adalat and the decree holder bank and did not pray for any rule against the judgment-debtor- petitioners and the said rule was made absolute on the ground that as the learned Advocate for the bank did not oppose the rule who submitted that he had instruction not to oppose the rule and accordingly supported the acceptance of the offer as made by writ petitioner which is a fraudulent game in between the writ petitioner and the bank and consequently "making the rule absolute on admission of one of the respondents is an error of law because a rule cannot be made absolute when it is not found that there was any error in the impugned order, more so, without hearing the petitioner, the aggrieved party in the action." 

 13. From the plaint as well as the decree passed in the suit, it appears that Messers the National Engineers Limited was impleaded as defendant No.1, Mohammad Hossain, its Managing Director, was impleaded as defendant No. 2 and after his death, his heirs, namely: 

 Sohrab Hossain, Nasima Hossain, Nazma Hossain were substituted as defendant Nos. 2(ka), (kha) and (ga). Mrs Hasina Hossain, wife of Mohammad Hossain, was impleaded in the suit as defendant No.3 and the decree was passed against them and thus they were the judgment-debtors and their properties were going to be sold in the auction sale, yet no Rule Nisi was issued against them. It appears from the impugned judgment and order that though on behalf of the Bank, i.e. writ- respondent No.2, an affidavit-in-opposition was filed at the hearing of the Rule Nisi, the learned . Advocate appearing for it made candid submission that he had instructions not to oppose the Rule Nisi and that the Bank was willing to accept the bid of the writ-petitioner and the Rule Nisi was made absolute on the said submissions of the learned Advocate for the Bank without saying anything as to the illegality or impropriety of the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat refusing to accept the bid offered by the writ-petitioner before declaring it to have been passed without lawful authority and was of no legal effect. 

 14. From the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which was impugned in the writ petition, it appears that the total price offered for the 3(three) scheduled properties advertised for auction sale was Taka 6,10,00,000 only, whereas the total dues of the judgment-debtor to the decree-holder Bank was Taka 22,35,15,053 from 1-10-1992 to 31-12-1992. The schedule of the properties advertised for sale was as follows: 

 16. In view of the area and the nature of the properties advertised for auction sale, the amount of claim of the decree-holder made in the execution case, the reasoning of the Artha Rin Adalat in refusing to accept the bid at Taka 6,10,00,000 only prima facie does not appear to us unreasonable and arbitrary. 

 18. It also raises a big question in our mind about the fairness and bonafide on the part of the decree-holder-Bank to file the application before the Artha Rin Adalat to accept the bid of the writ- petitioner at Taka 6,10,00,000 only and also as to the instruction given to its learned Advocate before the High Court Division not to oppose the Rule and its willingness to accept the bid at Taka 6 10 00 000 which was not even one third of its dues being Taka 22,35,15,053.
